newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's king warns against changes in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king warns against changes in Jerusalem.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein warned on Thursday against any new construction in Jerusalem which could pre-empt final negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians on the status of the holy city.

King Hussein, returning from a tour of Germany, Britain, Morocco and Ireland, said Jordan would voice concern "whenever we see something which might hinder our efforts...to build mutual confidence" in the Middle East.
He was responding to questions about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's plans to build 6,500 new homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.

"We are always in principle against any change in the status quo that might adversely affect any final outcome of the final negotiations over Jerusalem," the monarch told reporters after arriving in Amman.

On Wednesday, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat described as "completely illegal" Israeli plans to build in the eastern half of the city which he wants for the capital of a future Palestinian state.

Israeli left-wing critics of the project said it would spark Palestinian rage that could prove more costly than gunbattles in which 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died last year after Netanyahu opened a new entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.

The status of Jerusalem is to be decided along with other thorny issues -- such as Jewish settlements, Palestinian refugees and shape of Palestinian-Israeli borders -- in "final status" peace talks slated to restart next month.
